analysis.title: US Equity De-Grossing / Bessent On Fed Risk / Fed's Cook / SEC Probes Nvidia / Eurozone PMI
key_insights: UBS trading desk read Friday's US equity selling as de-grossing rather than capitulation. Composite volumes ran 60% above average with excess sell flow in both S&P and Nasdaq, and it felt like capitulation in semis and AI stocks.

Tech dispersion is rising. Software/cyber and select hyperscalers were better sponsored, while semiconductors and neoclouds were the main funding sources, so investors are differentiating on balance sheet and AI capex returns rather than abandoning the theme.
Retail turned seller of weakness. UBS retail market-making net flow fell to the lowest 7th percentile vs the last three years, with outflows in every sector led by Tech, and Nvidia inflows subsided.
Hedge funds remain defensive with little appetite to re-gross into year-end. Long-onlys monetised the bounce and have not chased strength, unlike the summer sell-off.

Systematic positioning is getting clean. CTA and risk-control funds are near their lowest quintile of exposure over five years and levered ETF exposure is effectively wiped out, so systematic supply should be a smaller downside driver.

Treasury Secretary Bessent said many worry the Fed could over-tighten. He blamed hawkish Fed communications and midterm results for last week's sell-off and questioned whether Nvidia was 'promiscuous' in chip sales.
Fed Governor Cook said policy is not restrictive enough and further tightening is needed. She said September's hike was not enough and financial conditions are too accommodative.

Nvidia fell more than 12% after Reuters reported an SEC enforcement accounting probe. DOJ is also reviewing the $12.9bn Hugging Face acquisition, and Megaspeed is under export-control investigation over alleged shipments of Nvidia chips to China.
Eurozone Composite PMI was unchanged at 51.7 in November, with manufacturing offsetting weaker services, and price indices fell. UK Composite PMI fell to 52.3 with services the drag.
SNB's Martin said inflation has kept rising and the December decision depends on the assessment at the moment, which the market read as hawkish.
Australia flash composite PMI fell to 46.1, the lowest since August 2021. NZ Q3 retail sales volumes rose 2.2% q/q vs 0.5% consensus, and UBS still sees an RBNZ 25bp hike in December.

US CCC spreads have widened six straight months, the longest run in 32 years outside a recession or crisis. They stand at 1,109bp as the 10y Treasury yield is 5.09% and CCC interest coverage has collapsed.
S&P 500 is down about 12% from its early October high. Record equity dispersion, the war in Iran, midterm results and shifting Fed guidance fed the sell-off while the VIX looked calm.
Kospi fell as much as 5.5% Monday after a 5.2% drop Friday despite stabilization measures. Authorities are preparing a stabilization fund and easing buyback limits.
Precious metals are in a relief rally driven by short-covering rather than new demand. Futures were the main source of supply and ETF holdings are the next test.

G10 FX: median G10 currency is down 260bp vs USD over ten days, below the 10th percentile of decade returns. USD-long positioning still looks light, and a further leg needs activity data and wider rate differentials.

Pre-market futures rebounded, with S&P futures up 2.8% and Nasdaq up 3.6%, after Friday's Nasdaq drop of 5.3% and the S&P's seventh straight daily loss. Heavy SOFR call spread and fly buying in 0QM7 showed as new risk.
EURUSD downside momentum has faded and the desk sees risk/reward skewed to a corrective move higher given stretched shorts. Topside pivot is 1.1015/20 and downside pivot 1.0940/50.
French rates are stalled with accounts raising cash for year-end and early-2027 supply, and insurers favour AAA agencies with 50-70bp pickup vs France.

tension_points.bull_case: Selling was de-grossing, not capitulation, and systematic positioning is clean so supply fades. Futures are sharply higher pre-market.
tension_points.bear_case: Discretionary conviction is extremely low, hedge funds will not re-gross, and long-onlys sell bounces. Burden of proof is on buyers chasing strength.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Buyers failing to chase strength and long-onlys continuing to monetise bounces.

theme_stances.key_argument: Selling reflected de-grossing with rising tech dispersion, and clean systematic positioning reduces downside supply.
Bessent warns of Fed over-tightening while Cook argues policy is not restrictive enough.
theme_stances.evidence: The current monetary policy stance is not providing needed restraint
